newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds headed towards a lower close on Tuesday with higher than expected U.S. housing starts pushing prices down in a quiet day of trading.
"Volume is so thin, the impact of the figures was felt quite strongly. With this degree of activity, it is noting special to have quite a bit of volitility," one dealer said.
Trade was thin and relatively uninspired, dealers said.

"We are focussed on the FOMC, really. If they decide to raise interest rates by a quarter (0.25 pct) today, there will be a lot going on in Amsterdam tomorrow. Everybody will have to cover their positions," another dealer said.
The market does not expect the Fed to act on the rates today as U.S. economic growth seems to be slowing down.

"As trade is extremely thin with mainly professional players left on the market, prices can show great movements if unexpected factors turn up or if somebody decides to do a big transaction, but for the moment it looks as if everything will be calm until next year," one dealer said.
